title: Tiered admission quarantine and geo-fence repair
author: Maya Chen
description: Background and motivation: In a recent incident we observed cascading slowpaths during a multi-zone storm where a combination of aggressive admission and aggressive regional failover caused noisy eviction and repeated circuit flips for medium-priority tenants. This change introduces a tiered admission quarantine: lightweight per-tenant probation windows (soft quarantine) followed by a short, telemetry-backed hard quarantine, plus a geo-fence correction that prevents duplicate egress-forced failovers when AZ probes disagree. The goal is to reduce SLO oscillation, improve stability during brief regional storms, and make on-call recovery less noisy. Implementation summary: 1) Introduce kidnap-resistant admission tiers in pkg/shedder/tenancy_shedder.go. Tiers: new_requests -> probation -> restricted -> suspended. Probation windows are exponential-backoff per-tenant and decay with successful requests. 2) Add a geo-fence reconciler in pkg/circuit/geo_fence.go that remembers the last proven healthy region per-tenant for a short TTL and disallows automated cross-region egress-switching if the destination region has fewer live success probes than a threshold. 3) Add a new circuit state transition metric (circuit_transition_reason) and a lightweight counter to avoid repeated flips: circuit_manager.go includes a 60s sticky window with graded decay. 4) Add a short-lived oncall probe and runbook under cmd/oncall-probes/ to help SRE manually unstick tenants during rollouts. 5) Observer changes: observability/alerts/slo.yml adds an alert for "SLO-flutter-rate" (rate of tenant-level SLO regressions) and a dashboard panel for probation window occupancy. 6) Tests: tests/e2e/geo_quarantine_test.go simulates flapping AZ probe signals and verifies no more than one forced egress-redirection within a 3-minute window for a tenant; unit tests cover tier promotion/demotion logic. Rollout and migration plan: - Phase 1 (canary, 10% hosts, region A): enable the tiered admission default with probation windows set conservatively (min probation 6s, max 90s). Monitor SLO-flutter-rate and probation occupancy. - Phase 2 (regional ramp): expand to 50% of traffic; if SLO-flutter-rate drops by >25% and no increase in successful-request median latency >5ms, enable geo-fence enforcement. - Phase 3 (global): full rollout with current defaults. Feature flagging: all behavior gated behind feature flag service.feature.tiered_quarantine; geo-fence gated under service.feature.geo_fence_reconciler. Backout plan: flip flags off; circuit_manager sticky window will naturally decay. Observability and telemetry: added histogram for probation_duration_seconds, counter for probation_promotes and probation_demotes, gauge for probation_occupancy_by_tier. Alerts added for SLO-flutter-rate and geo-fence-mismatch-count. Related issues: links to incident notes and SUP-1284 and ENG-4521. Checklist: - [x] Design doc reviewed by SRE and Runtime teams - [x] Unit tests added (coverage +4%) - [x] E2E simulation added - [x] Feature flags in place - [x] Runbook + oncall probe included - [x] Dashboard + alert created - [x] Canary rollout plan documented Possible risks and mitigations: - Overly conservative probation windows could delay legitimate traffic: mitigated by conservative defaults and rapid toggle via feature flags. - Geo-fence may hide genuine multi-region failovers: reconciler tracks recent probe success ratios and logs decisions; we instrumented telemetry to surface suppressed failovers. Security and compliance: no secret or policy changes. No breaking API changes. Merge notes: squashed commits into a single logical change and added an expanded commit message for release notes.

review_comments:
Arjun Patel: Please explain the decay math for the probation window in more detail. Concern: exponential backoff could penalize bursty legitimate tenants.
Maya Chen (author): We use clipped exponential with a per-tenant success-based fast-path reset. If a tenant has 3 consecutive successful requests inside probation we reset to min_proba (6s). The decay factors and clips are in the comments of tenancy_shedder.go.

Diego Morales: The geo_fence TTL seems short (30s). On under-provisioned regions probes can bounce. Can we make it adaptive?
Maya Chen: Good call. I added an adaptive_ttl = min(max(30s, 2 * median_probe_rtt), 180s) — implementation in geo_fence.go. I also added unit tests to verify behavior across RTTs.

Sofia Alvarez: Integration test flaked once in CI (e2e simulated race). Did we stabilize it?
Maya Chen: The flake came from a time-based assertion; I adjusted the test to wait for a stable window and added a retry harness. CI re-run passed.

Arjun Patel: Please include a short note in runbook for manual unstick steps.
Maya Chen: Done — cmd/oncall-probes/runbook.md includes the commands to clear probation and force a safe egress redirect.

Diego Morales: Approving after CI green and docs update.

merge_commit_message: Tiered admission quarantine + geo-fence reconciler: reduce SLO oscillation during regional storms. (ENG-4521, SUP-1284)
release_notes: Introduce tiered admission quarantine (probation -> restricted -> suspended) and geo-fence reconciler to stabilize regional failovers; added SLO-flutter-rate alert and runbook. Backward compatible behind feature flags.
notes_for_oncall: If a tenant is stuck in suspended state after rollout, use oncall-probes/unstick --tenant <id> to clear probation and optionally force egress; if geo-fence suppresses a legitimate failover, flip feature.feature.geo_fence_reconciler off and observe for 10m. Monitor SLO-flutter-rate and probation_occupancy_by_tier.
